name: FL-17
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about 10 points on recent partisan performance
Incumbent Greg Steube holds a roughly 14-to-1 fundraising and cash advantage over Matthew Montavon
Prediction markets price a Republican win at about 94-95 percent
No public polling of the race; the Democratic challenger remains little known and minimally funded
model.rationale: The seat's strong Republican lean, Steube's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets pricing his reelection near 95 percent all point to a comfortable Republican hold; with no polling available, uncertainty stays elevated, but the structural evidence is one-sided.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Steube or a sharply favorable Democratic national environment would be the main forces that could narrow this margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 17th District, covering parts of southwest Florida including Sarasota and Charlotte counties, leans Republican by about ten points based on recent partisan performance. Republican Greg Steube, first elected in 2018, is seeking another term after securing renomination. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised roughly $1.3 million and holding more than $2 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Matthew Montavon has raised about $96,000. An independent candidate is also on the ballot but minimally funded.

No public polls of the race are available, and national race raters have not published individual assessments. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 94 percent chance of winning. The combination of the district's lean, the incumbent's resources, and the challenger's limited campaign points to a comfortable Republican hold, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling in the contest.
